newsitem.title: CANADA: Reuters bond pricing appeal postponed.
newsitem.headline: Reuters bond pricing appeal postponed.

text.p: The Ontario Securities Commission on Thursday postponed a hearing to decide whether Reuters Holdings Plc can provide bond pricing services in Canada.

The provincial securities regulator said it adjourned the June 9 hearing at the request of Reuters and the Investment Dealers Association of Canada. The hearing is expected to be rescheduled for August.

The OSC said both Reuters and the IDA had requested the adjournment "to allow them and their counsel an opportunity to further address matters relating to Reuters' RMTO (recognized market transparency organization) application."
The IDA in January rejected an application by Reuters to provide Canadian bond pricing services in competition with CanPX Corp.

CanPX was set up by the IDA with the goal of making the Canadian bond market more transparent. The creation of CanPX would require interdealer bond brokers to provide real-time market prices, volumes and other information to the tranparency organization.
Approving the creation of CanPX last year, the OSC said the IDA had the right to approve competing tranparency organizations.

Reuters' was the only company that applied to compete with CanPX. However, in rejecting Reuters' application, the IDA said the company had "failed to demonstrate satisfactorily that it can perform transparency-related services as effectively as CanPX."
A Reuters spokesman said at the time the company was disappointed by the decision and that an appeal to the OSC could be expected.
